title: Confidence-Weighted Self-Distillation for Learning under Label Noise

evaluation.resolution: measured.<arm>.<metric> resolves to measured[arm][str(seed)][metric] in measured.json, written by run_all_arms.sh from each run's --metrics-out JSON. The arm keys are exactly claims.json['arms']; a reserved _meta key at the top level of measured.json is ignored by the gate.
evaluation.ordering: the quantity must satisfy `direction` at EVERY seed.
evaluation.value: abs(quantity - claimed) <= tolerance at EVERY seed.
evaluation.existence_or_invariant: the boolean predicate (an expression over measured.<arm>.<metric> tokens, with min(), max(), mean(), abs(), arithmetic, comparisons, and/or) must evaluate true at EVERY seed. Structural invariants are emitted as measured metrics by run_experiment.py --metrics-out (Eqs. 1-4) AND independently checked by pytest (the claim's `check`); the predicate is the measured-expression form, the `check` is the test-suite form. A grader that cannot run raises; a missing/BLOCKED metric blocks the claim rather than fabricating a verdict.

compute_invariance.policy: high = the assertion is structural (independent of the 4000-step training budget: gate bounds, simplex membership, stop-grad, single-network, degeneracy) or a sign-only ordering that survives seed changes; low = an exact magnitude that the paper reports for a single seed-0 run and that the split/noise/init seed-dependence perturbs. The numbers gate checks the HIGH claims.

baseline.name: Cross-entropy (baseline)

metrics.accuracy: Held-out test accuracy in [0,1] on the clean, class-stratified 30% split (540 examples), from the 'FINAL accuracy=<float>' line (paper/paper.md:466-470). Headline metric.
metrics.param_count: Number of parameter tensors {W1,b1,W2,b2}; ==4 (single network, no extra params; paper/paper.md:21-23).
metrics.gate_w_min: Min over a batch of w=lam*sigmoid((c-tau)/s) (Eq. 2); ==0 at lambda=0 (degeneracy anchor).
metrics.gate_w_max: Max over a batch of w; ==0 at lambda=0 (w identically zero, t==y).
metrics.degeneracy_loss_err: |loss(lambda=0) - independent cross-entropy loss| on a batch; exactly 0.0 (paper/paper.md:253-280, 'recovers the cross-entropy baseline exactly').
metrics.degeneracy_grad_err: max|grad(lambda=0) - independent CE grad| over all four params; exactly 0.0.

baseline.notes: Paper Table 1 first row (paper/paper.md:400-406). Same program as CWSD with --lambda 0.0; tau, s and temperature are inert at lambda=0 because w is identically 0 (paper/paper.md:253-280). The degeneracy_*_err metrics ARE the paper's own verification gate (lambda=0 reproduces the baseline exactly), measured as a bitwise comparison to an independently written cross-entropy routine.

cwsd.name: CWSD (ours)

metrics.accuracy: Held-out test accuracy in [0,1] on the clean, class-stratified 30% split (540 examples), from the 'FINAL accuracy=<float>' line. Headline metric.
metrics.param_count: Number of parameter tensors {W1,b1,W2,b2}; ==4 (single network, no extra params; paper/paper.md:21-23).
metrics.gate_w_min: Min over a batch of w=lam*sigmoid((c-tau)/s) (Eq. 2); >0 for lambda>0 (sigmoid is strictly positive).
metrics.gate_w_max: Max over a batch of w; <lambda=1 (sigmoid<1), so w<1 (paper/paper.md:114-125 'maximum influence self-distillation may have').
metrics.target_min: Min t_ik over a batch (Eq. 3); >=0 (t is a convex combination of two distributions, both >=0).
metrics.target_sum_err: max|sum_k t_ik - 1| over a batch; ~1e-7 (t is a convex combination of two distributions, both summing to 1; paper/paper.md:172-176).
metrics.stopgrad_grad_err: max|hand-derived grad - central finite-diff grad| on a tiny network; ~1e-3 (float32 finite-diff noise). Proves dL/dz=(p-t)/B with t constant (Eq. 3 stop-grad; paper/paper.md:213-214).

cwsd.notes: Paper Table 1 second row (paper/paper.md:408-414). lambda=1, tau=0.9, T=2 are stated (paper/paper.md:361-377); s=0.15 is calibrated because the paper never states the gate sharpness (SPEC.md section 4 item 1). The structural metrics (gate_w_*, target_*, stopgrad_grad_err, param_count) are the measured evidence for the paper's equation-invariants.

claims.quote: CWSD improves over the cross-entropy baseline (Table 1 caption; on disk the sentence reads 'CWSD improves over the cross-entropy baseline by 2.5 accuracy points.' across lines 420-427 with the spaced token stream '2 . 5')
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:420-427 (grep 'improves over the cross-entropy' resolves to line 420)
claims.arithmetic: (measured.cwsd.accuracy - measured.baseline.accuracy) > 0, evaluated at every seed in [0, 1, 2]. This is the paper's central claim and the one the reproduction gates on; it asks for a sign only, so it survives a smaller compute budget.

claims.quote: Cross-entropy (baseline) 0 0.9370 (Table 1, first row; tokens 'Cross-entropy (baseline)', '0', '0', '.', '9370' on lines 400-406)
claims.arithmetic: abs(measured.baseline.accuracy - 0.9370) <= 0.01 at every seed. Exact magnitudes do not survive seed changes (the paper reports a single seed-0 run), hence low compute-invariance; the tolerance covers the paper's number plus five test examples on the 540-example test set.

claims.quote: CWSD (ours) 1 0.9620 (Table 1, second row; tokens 'CWSD (ours)', '1', '0', '.', '9620' on lines 408-414)
claims.arithmetic: abs(measured.cwsd.accuracy - 0.9620) <= 0.015 at every seed. Low compute-invariance for the same reason as baseline-accuracy-value.

claims.quote: it improves test accuracy by 2.5 points over standard cross-entropy. (Abstract; on disk 'by', '2', '.', '5', 'points over standard', 'cross-entropy' span lines 28-36)
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:28-36 (grep 'points over standard' resolves to line 34)
claims.arithmetic: abs((measured.cwsd.accuracy - measured.baseline.accuracy) - 0.025) <= 0.02 at every seed. The gap's magnitude is seed-sensitive; the paper tested only seed 0, so the tolerance spans the observed seed spread. The robust claim is the ordering (cwsd-improves-over-baseline), not the exact 2.5 points.

claims.quote: Setting the mixing coefficient to zero recovers the cross-entropy baseline exactly
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:35-36 (grep 'recovers the cross-entropy baseline exactly' resolves to line 35; see also the method-section restatement at paper/paper.md:253-280, grep 'strict generalisation')

claims.quote: scaled by a coefficient lambda in [0,1] that sets the maximum influence self-distillation may have
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:114-125 (grep 'maximum influence' resolves to line 125; Eq. (2) at paper/paper.md:127-158)

claims.quote: The training target is the convex combination of the label and the model's own temperature-softened prediction
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:172-176 (grep 'convex combination' resolves to line 172; Eq. (3) at paper/paper.md:178-212)

claims.quote: The stop-gradient is essential: without it the target follows the prediction and the objective admits a trivial solution.
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:213-214 (grep 'trivial solution' resolves to line 214; 'stopgrad' appears at line 198 in Eq. (3))

claims.quote: CWSD adds one forward pass of bookkeeping, no second network, and no additional parameters.
claims.citation: paper/paper.md:21-23 (grep 'no second network' resolves to line 23)

not_tested.quote: We attribute the gain to the gate suppressing the gradient contribution of examples whose labels disagree with a confident prediction, which are disproportionately the corrupted ones.
not_tested.citation: paper/paper.md:443-447 (grep 'We attribute the gain' resolves to line 443)
not_tested.reason: Mechanism/attribution claim, phrased by the paper itself as an attribution ('We attribute'), not a measured result. Testing it requires per-example gate-weight logging that the paper's output contract (one 'FINAL accuracy=' line, paper/paper.md:466-470) does not expose; intentionally left out of the gate.

not_tested.quote: All results are single runs at seed 0
not_tested.citation: paper/paper.md:385-389 (grep 'single runs at seed' resolves to line 385)
not_tested.reason: The paper's exact Table-1 magnitudes are seed-0 runs of a pipeline in which the split, noise mask, and init all depend on the seed. Value-type claims at seeds 1 and 2 are therefore out-of-distribution for the paper's numbers and are covered by widened tolerances rather than asserted as reproductions at those seeds.
